```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5, dpi = 120)
source("../R/_load.R")
```

```{r load}
df <- readRDS(file.path(cfg$paths$out, "data", "analysis_data.rds"))
fm <- model_formula(cfg); m1 <- fit_survey_logit(df, fm); or1 <- label_terms(tidy_or(m1$fit, m1$design), cfg$analysis$covariates)
```

## 1. Complete-case analysis

Structural categories ("not asked") are kept in the primary model. The complete-case run drops them.

```{r cc}
cc <- df[df$complete_case, ]; mcc <- fit_survey_logit(cc, fm)
orcc <- label_terms(tidy_or(mcc$fit, mcc$design), cfg$analysis$covariates)
cmp <- merge(or1[, c("term", "or")], orcc[, c("term", "or", "ci_low", "ci_high")], by = "term", suffixes = c("_primary", "_complete_case"))
save_table(cmp, "07_complete_case", cfg); knitr::kable(cmp, digits = 2)
```

## 2. Alternative adequacy thresholds

```{r thr}
d <- df[df$in_sample, ]
thr <- lapply(c(3, 4, 5, 6, 8), function(k) { d$y <- as.numeric(d$anc_visits >= k); dd <- d; dd$adequate_anc <- dd$y
  m <- fit_survey_logit(dd, fm); o <- label_terms(tidy_or(m$fit, m$design), cfg$analysis$covariates); o$threshold <- k; o })
thr <- bind_rows(thr); thr <- thr[!is.na(thr$variable), ]; save_table(thr, "07_thresholds", cfg)
knitr::kable(thr[thr$variable %in% c("Education", "Wealth quintile") & grepl("Higher|Richest", thr$category), c("threshold", "variable", "category", "or", "ci_low", "ci_high")], digits = 2)
```

## 3. Influence of the largest counties and of single counties

Leave-one-county-out estimates of the education and wealth odds ratios show whether a single county drives the result.

```{r loo}
cn <- sort(unique(as.character(d$county)))
loo <- bind_rows(lapply(cn, function(k) { dd <- d[as.character(d$county) != k, ]; m <- fit_survey_logit(dd, fm)
  o <- tidy_or(m$fit, m$design); o$dropped <- k; o[o$term %in% c("educationHigher", "wealthRichest"), ] }))
save_table(loo, "07_leave_one_county_out", cfg)
rng <- loo |> group_by(term) |> summarise(min_or = min(or), max_or = max(or), full_or = or1$or[match(first(term), or1$term)])
knitr::kable(rng, digits = 2)
```

## 4. Weighted versus unweighted logistic regression

```{r unw}
mu <- glm(fm, data = m1$data, family = binomial); ouw <- label_terms(data.frame(term = names(coef(mu)), or_unweighted = exp(coef(mu))), cfg$analysis$covariates)
cmp2 <- merge(or1[, c("term", "or")], ouw[, c("term", "or_unweighted")], by = "term"); save_table(cmp2, "07_weighted_vs_unweighted", cfg); knitr::kable(cmp2, digits = 2)
```

## 5. Design effects

```{r deff}
ds <- subset(make_design(d), TRUE)
de <- survey::svymean(~adequate_anc, ds, deff = "replace"); deff <- data.frame(estimate = coef(de), se = survey::SE(de), deff = survey::deff(de))
save_table(deff, "07_design_effect", cfg); knitr::kable(deff, digits = 3)
```

## 6. Residual spatial dependence in the survey-weighted model

```{r resid_moran}
if (file.exists(cfg$paths$boundaries)) {
  sp <- readRDS(file.path(cfg$paths$out, "data", "spatial_results.rds"))
  dm <- m1$data; dm$res <- residuals(glm(fm, data = dm, family = binomial), type = "response")
  cr <- dm |> group_by(county_key = norm_name(county)) |> summarise(r = mean(res))
  nb <- build_neighbours(sp$bnd, cfg); r <- cr$r[match(sp$bnd$county_key, cr$county_key)]
  knitr::kable(global_moran(r, nb$lw, cfg$spatial$permutations, cfg$project$seed), digits = 4)
}
```
